prompt: A machine has peak compute 2,000 GFLOP/s and memory bandwidth 200 GB/s. A compute kernel has arithmetic intensity 0.5 FLOP/byte. What is its upper bound under the two-ceiling roofline model?

options.explanation: That is the flat compute roof. At the stated intensity of 0.5 FLOP per byte, the compute kernel is far to the left of the ridge (10 FLOP/byte), on the sloped bandwidth roof.
This divides bandwidth by AI (200 / 0.5). The bandwidth roof multiplies intensity by bandwidth.
This multiplies peak by AI. The memory roof depends on bandwidth, not on peak compute.
Correct. The bandwidth roof is 0.5 × 200 = 100 GFLOP/s, below the 2,000 GFLOP/s compute roof: a bandwidth ceiling at 5% of peak. Actual performance may be lower.

workedExample:
```formula
AI_r = P / B = 2,000 / 200 = 10
P_att = min(P, AI × B)
P_att = min(2,000, 0.5 × 200)
P_att = min(2,000, 100) = 100
where
AI_r: the ridge-point intensity, in FLOP per byte
P: peak compute; 2,000 GFLOP/s
B: memory bandwidth; 200 GB/s
P_att: the attainable bound, in GFLOP/s
AI: the compute kernel's arithmetic intensity; 0.5 FLOP per byte
min: the smaller of its inputs
In words: at 0.5 FLOP per byte, 200 GB/s can feed only 100 GFLOP/s, far below the 2,000 GFLOP/s peak.
```

Every byte delivered supports half a FLOP, and the machine delivers 200 GB/s. No amount of SIMD tuning lifts this compute kernel above 100 GFLOP/s; only raising its intensity (or the bandwidth) can.

prompt: A GPU offers 20 TFLOP/s and 1 TB/s of memory bandwidth. Where is its ridge point, and which of the two roofline ceilings is lower at an arithmetic intensity (AI) of 4 FLOP/byte?

options.text: Ridge at 0.05 FLOP/byte; the compute kernel is compute-bound
options.explanation: This inverts the required ratio. Dividing the stated compute peak by bandwidth gives a ridge at 20 FLOP per byte.

options.text: Ridge at 20 FLOP/byte; bandwidth is the lower ceiling, at 4 TFLOP/s
options.explanation: Correct. 20 × 10¹² / 1 × 10¹² = 20. At AI 4 the compute kernel is left of the ridge: 4 × 1 TB/s = 4 TFLOP/s, 20% of peak.

options.text: Ridge at 20 FLOP/byte; the compute kernel is compute-bound because 4 FLOP/byte is a high intensity
options.explanation: Whether an AI is "high" depends on the machine. 4 FLOP/byte is below this GPU's ridge of 20, so the bandwidth roof is the limit.

options.text: Ridge at 4 FLOP/byte; the compute kernel sits exactly at the ridge
options.explanation: The ridge follows the ratio of the selected compute and bandwidth ceilings, rather than the individual compute kernel’s intensity.

workedExample:
```formula
AI_r = P / B
AI_r = (20 × 10^12) / 10^12 = 20
P_bw = AI × B = 4 × 10^12
where
AI_r: the ridge point, in FLOP per byte
P: peak compute; 20 TFLOP/s = 20 × 10^12 FLOP per second
B: memory bandwidth; 1 TB/s = 10^12 bytes per second
P_bw: the bandwidth ceiling at this intensity, in FLOP per second (4 × 10^12 is 4 TFLOP/s)
AI: the compute kernel's arithmetic intensity; 4 FLOP per byte
In words: the ridge is at 20 FLOP per byte; at 4 the memory roof of 4 TFLOP/s is the lower ceiling.
```

The bandwidth ceiling of 4 TFLOP/s is below the 20 TFLOP/s arithmetic ceiling. A measured compute kernel may run lower for other reasons. Compare the selected precision and a consistent traffic definition before choosing an optimisation.
